mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -58.7% in the most recent week after a three-week trend of marginal improvement (-61.1% to -58.7%). This stabilization signals the floor of demand contraction has been reached, and mean-reversion over the next four weeks will drive RETAIL_REC higher than the preceding four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 2.4 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -58.7% or declines further below -60%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has recovered 4.3 points from t-3w to t-0w (-28.7% to -24.4%), indicating consumers are normalizing essential shopping patterns. This normalization of essential-goods mobility will spill over into discretionary retail within two weeks as confidence in mobility safety increases.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -28.7% to -24.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM recovery, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses below -26% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered 2.6 points from t-3w to t-0w (-52.7% to -50.1%), signaling partial return of commuting. Concurrent with this, TRANSIT has improved 3.4 points (-57.3% to -53.9%), indicating coordinated mobility recovery. The interaction of workplace and transit recovery will drive retail footfall upward over four weeks as commute-linked shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve more than 2 points in same week
evidence_refs: fact:both improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses below their t-3w levels within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed -58.7% on average over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained elevated and stable (13.0% to 14.3%) across all four weeks, indicating sustained stay-at-home behavior. If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 13% in the next week, it signals policy restrictions remain in force, constraining RETAIL_REC to remain below -55% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 13% in the next observed week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at 13.0-14.3% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 12% within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -55% on average over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered 4.6 points from t-3w to t-1w (-20.9% to -16.3%), then reverted to -20.9% at t-0w. This volatility in outdoor recreation signals uncertainty in activity patterns. If PARKS volatility persists (week-on-week swings > 3 points), RETAIL_REC will remain depressed below -58% over the next four weeks due to inconsistent consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exhibits week-on-week volatility exceeding 3 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -16.3% to -20.9% between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS stabilizes within a 2-point band for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -57% on average over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between RETAIL_REC (-58.7%) and GROCERY_PHARM (-24.4%) has widened to 34.3 points, the largest in the four-week window. This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essential goods over discretionary retail. Closure of this gap requires RETAIL_REC to rise faster than GROCERY_PHARM over the next two weeks; failure to narrow the gap signals persistent demand weakness.
failure_condition: The gap narrows by more than 10 points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -54% while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -22%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved 3.4 points over four weeks (-57.3% to -53.9%), but remains severely depressed. If TRANSIT fails to improve by at least 2 additional points in the next week, it signals public-transport confidence has plateaued, constraining RETAIL_REC recovery to less than 2 points of improvement over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement falls below 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.4 points over four weeks but remains at -53.9%
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by 2 or more points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC improves by more than 2 points on average over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL exhibit a coordinated pattern: workplace and transit recovery coupled with sustained residential elevation. This three-way interaction indicates a hybrid work regime where partial commuting coexists with home-based activity. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will improve by 1-3 points over four weeks as hybrid workers make targeted shopping trips, but will not exceed -56%.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves, TRANSIT improves, and RESIDENTIAL remains above 13%
evidence_refs: fact:all three show coordinated movement over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 3 points on average, or RESIDENTIAL drops below 12% while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stagnate.
